w10_T4_002724: Lucia's cake shop had 73 orders on its books on Monday. On Tuesday 48 new orders came in, and on Wednesday 51 orders were cancelled. On Thursday 66 more orders arrived, and on Friday another 31. Each cupcake in an order sells for 2 dollars. Every order is for 3 cupcakes, and her rival Marco had fewer orders on his books that week. How many cupcakes does Lucia need to bake for the week's orders?
w10_T4_002732: A market stall started the day with 25 crates of melons and sold 19 crates to a restaurant. The stallholder then received a delivery that tripled the number of crates on the stall. Every crate holds 7 melons, so she unpacked them all onto the counter. The stall is 4 metres wide. She threw away 27 bruised melons and sold 55 more by closing time. How many melons were left on the counter?
w10_T4_002735: A parent baked 84 muffins and split them equally among the 6 classes at Oakfield School. In Ms. Ortiz's class, the children ate 12 of their muffins at snack time. Later the class received 20 more muffins from the office, and then gave 12 muffins to Mr. Bell's class next door, which had fewer muffins than Ms. Ortiz's class. The muffins Ms. Ortiz's class still had were shared equally among the 5 tables in her room, and the children at each table cut every one of their muffins into 5 pieces. How many pieces of muffin were on the first table?
w10_T4_002741: In the morning a flower seller had 30 bunches of lilies, and 18 wilted bunches had to be thrown out. In the afternoon a delivery brought 48 fresh bunches. Each bunch held 5 stems, so she untied them all and displayed the stems singly, adding 61 loose stems left over from another order. In the evening she sold every stem on the display at 8 dollars each. How many dollars did she take in that evening?
w10_T4_002743: In the morning Aiden set off with 105 flyers for the school play and handed out 79 of them outside the station. In the afternoon he handed out 24 more at the shopping centre, and 1 flyer blew away in the wind. In the evening the drama teacher gave him a fresh bundle of 42 flyers for the next day. His friend Zoe handed out fewer flyers than Aiden that day. How many flyers did Aiden have at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002745: Farida had 69 stickers and used 60 of them to decorate a poster. She shared the stickers she had left equally among herself, Rana, and Tariq, so each of the 3 friends got the same number. Half an hour later Farida opened a new pack and added 51 stickers to her share. She then traded 41 stickers to Tariq for a comic and received 22 stickers from her teacher. Rana finished the day with fewer stickers than Farida. How many stickers does Farida have now?
w10_T4_002749: The community fridge on Elm Street held 89 packed meals on Monday morning. During the day 42 meals were taken by neighbours, and a dozen volunteers removed 10 meals that had passed their date. On Tuesday a restaurant donated 48 meals to the fridge. On Wednesday 74 meals were taken, and 3 were dropped and had to be thrown out. How many meals are in the fridge now?
w10_T4_002753: In the morning a parking garage held 186 cars. By ten o'clock 58 cars had driven out and 5 had driven in. In the afternoon another 80 cars left. In the evening 61 cars arrived for the theatre show next door, which ran for one hundred and twenty minutes, that is, two hours. How many cars were in the garage at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002760: A school ordered 155 boxes of pencils for its dozen classrooms, but 31 boxes never arrived. Every box that did arrive held 8 pencils, and the caretaker tipped them all into one big drawer. He found that 11 pencils were broken and threw them away. During the term 799 pencils were handed out to students, and 9 pencils were later handed back in. How many pencils are in the drawer now?
w10_T4_002764: In the morning Sara arrived at the water park with 173 dollars, and her mother gave her 18 dollars more at the gate. She changed all of her dollars into wristband credits at 2 credits per dollar, in a queue that took two hours, one hundred and twenty minutes. She then won 70 credits in a splash contest. In the afternoon she divided all her credits into 2 equal shares and gave one share to her cousin Nico. In the evening she found 26 credits she had forgotten in her bag and added them to her share. How many credits did Sara have at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002765: A courier named Ali drives 101 kilometres a day, 7 days a week, and kept that up for 4 weeks. On top of that he made a 21-kilometre detour to a depot and a 70-kilometre trip for a special delivery. His van holds 60 litres of fuel. When he handed in his logbook, 1324 kilometres were struck off as personal driving that the company does not pay for. His colleague Ben was paid for fewer kilometres than Ali that month. How many kilometres was Ali paid for?
w10_T4_002767: A farmer filled 7 sacks with 35 kilograms of seed grain each and stored them in one bin. A neighbour added 79 kilograms of seed to the bin, and a cooperative sent 80 kilograms more. Every kilogram of seed in the bin was sown, and every kilogram sown yielded 6 kilograms of grain at harvest. The grain sold for 9 cents per kilogram, which the farmer tallied in cents even though a hundred cents make a dollar. The proceeds were then split into 2 equal shares, one for the farmer and one for the landlord. How many cents did the farmer's share come to?
w10_T4_002771: In the morning Greta picked strawberries from her 5 rows of 197 plants each, and every plant gave 8 ripe berries. She set aside 1885 bruised berries for jam. In the afternoon she sold every remaining berry at the market for 5 cents each. In the evening a customer came back and gave her a 55-cent tip. Her neighbour Paul earned less at the market than Greta. How many cents did Greta take in altogether?
w10_T4_002778: Nate is tiling a floor and has 30 boxes of mosaic tiles; each box contains 8 packs, and each pack holds 4 tiles. He also has 26 loose tiles from an earlier job in the same pile. For the border pattern he cuts every tile in the pile into 3 equal strips. He then lays 1440 strips along the border. His colleague Rosa has fewer strips left than Nate. How many strips does Nate have left?
w10_T4_002786: Priya's video-calling plan started the month with 193 minutes. She used 13 minutes on a call to her bank, and the provider then added a 37-minute bonus. She spent 129 minutes on calls to her sister, bought a 64-minute top-up, and then used 112 minutes on a family call. The plan costs 20 dollars a month. Priya knows sixty minutes make an hour, but the plan counts everything in minutes. How many minutes does Priya have left?
w10_T4_002787: In the morning 205 runners lined up for the city half-marathon, and 19 latecomers joined them just before the start, followed by 31 more who had queued at the wrong gate. Every runner took 4 cups of water from the dozen water stations along the course. The winner finished in one hundred and twenty minutes, that is, two hours. In the afternoon the volunteers drank 65 cups themselves while packing up, and in the evening the cleanup crew used 29 more cups. How many cups were used in total that day?
w10_T4_002788: In the morning 110 people were waiting in the clinic's waiting room. By mid-morning 27 had been seen and sent home, and another 39 had been seen after that, a stretch that took the nurses three hours, one hundred and eighty minutes. In the afternoon the people still waiting were split into 2 equal groups and one group was moved to the annex. The group left in the waiting room was then split again into 2 equal groups, and one of those groups was called through to the doctors. In the evening 39 new patients arrived in the waiting room. How many people were in the waiting room at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002792: A library book drive collected 194 books in its first week, then 59 more, then 45 more, and finally 74 more. The drive lasted 5 weeks in all. The librarians sorted all the donated books into 3 equal piles and sent one pile to the children's room. For every book in that pile, the children's librarian bought a second copy, so the children's room ended up with 2 copies of each of those books. Then 45 of the books in the children's room were lent out on the first day. How many of the children's-room books were still on the shelves?
w10_T4_002794: In the morning Nikhil opened his chai stall and sold 45 cups in each of the 9 hours until mid-afternoon. In the afternoon rush he sold 15 more cups, and then another 28 cups to a tour group. In the evening he tallied up: every cup he had sold that day was priced at 3 dollars. His cousin Meera's stall sold fewer cups than Nikhil's. How many dollars did Nikhil take in that day?
w10_T4_002797: Grandma baked 228 cookies on Saturday and 52 more on Sunday, a job that took her one hundred and fifty minutes, two and a half hours. She shared all the cookies equally among her 5 grandchildren. Lila ate 25 of her cookies straight away. Her brother Ben, who did not like the raisin ones, gave Lila 53 cookies from his share, so Ben ended up with fewer cookies than Lila. How many cookies does Lila have now?
w10_T4_002802: In the morning Jamal sold 50 tickets an hour for 4 hours for the school play. Before lunch 25 tickets were refunded, and 4 tickets were lost in the office and voided. In the afternoon the treasurer counted the sale as 3 dollars for every valid ticket. The play ran for ninety minutes, an hour and a half. In the evening Jamal paid 494 dollars of costume costs out of the ticket money. His co-organiser Kim raised fewer dollars than Jamal. How many dollars did Jamal have left after paying the costs?
w10_T4_002804: A candle maker had 106 boxes with 6 candles in each. She sold 299 candles at a fair and donated 164 candles to a church, leaving the rest on half a shelf in her workshop. Each of her candles burns for 7 hours, and every hour of burning uses 9 grams of wax. How many grams of wax will the candles she has left use up if they all burn out completely?
w10_T4_002805: In the morning Lin picked 17 baskets of apples from the orchard, with 7 apples in every basket. Her friend Mo, who picked fewer apples than Lin, gave her 19 apples from his own basket. In the afternoon Lin sold 127 apples at the roadside stall. In the evening she cut every apple she had left into 7 slices for a pie. How many apple slices did Lin have for the pie?
w10_T4_002807: In the morning Elena collected 19 empty bottles along the beach, and 43 more by the pier. In the afternoon she gathered 68 bottles near the car park and 78 bottles by the picnic tables, keeping everything in one sack. In the evening she took the sack to the recycling machine, which paid 5 cents for every bottle. She then found 39 cents in the coin tray and added it to her refund. How many cents did Elena end up with?
w10_T4_002809: In the morning a bakery had 129 bread rolls on its shelves and took 37 more out of the oven. By the afternoon a big bake had tripled the number of rolls on the shelves, and a neighbour returned 14 rolls she had bought by mistake, which went back on the shelves. In the evening every roll on the shelves was sold to a canteen at 5 cents each. The bakery then paid 2139 cents for the flour it had used. How many cents did the bakery have left from the sale?
